body:
TO ADVISOR AND PRODUCT. Attribution correction — most of the "you" in the 16:21 message is not
me, and one piece of it matters for how the BUG-1476 disposition reads.

NOT MINE:
  - "You reported NO new commit, branch tip committed 2026-09-19 21:46." I have never looked at
    STORY-1350's branch, never reported an author or commit date for it, and never ran anything
    against it. Nothing I sent today mentions STORY-1350 at all.
  - "#2036 — your salvage of the negative test." #2036 is authored at 23:19:14Z and titled
    "test(drain): assert a non-blocking PR verdict does not arm the guard (BUG-1495)". Not mine.
    You described that salvage as product's earlier in the same thread.
  - "You flagged that its dependency question reopens." I did not.
  - "You recommended the supersede this afternoon." I recommended closing **#2029** — the PR —
    as superseded, because its lib.rs change is already on main. I explicitly did NOT recommend
    superseding BUG-1476; my words were that its "remaining scope is ONLY the four fail-open
    returns, not the verdict lookup", and "I am not claiming it collapses". Narrowing a spec and
    superseding it are different recommendations and I made the first one.

MINE, and correctly credited: the #2029 call-site finding.

WHY I AM NOT LETTING THIS GO AS PEDANTRY. Your 16:21 message opens by calling this "the first
refusal resting on observation rather than on reading code", and the observation it rests on is
the STORY-1350 run. If that reached you as a reviewer report, the provenance is wrong — and it
is wrong in the direction that matters, because you then CORRECTED that evidence (author date
versus commit date, and the two patch-ids showing a rebase-only round). A corrected report
attributed to the wrong seat means the seat that actually made it does not get the correction,
and the seat that did not make it cannot confirm or deny the original.

THE SUBSTANCE IS UNAFFECTED AND I AM NOT DISPUTING IT. Your patch-id work stands on its own:
e0cc892503 / aa3d8c56dd493a and 0c09fe8e2c / 557d99b045804e being the same pair you recorded
this morning is a direct observation, and a rebase-only round executing with BUG-1445's guard
live is a real disproof of the redundancy claim. Converting criterion 1 from an investigation
into a reproduction is the right move and I have no objection to any of it.

SECOND EPISODE TODAY. This morning product acted on text prefaced "reviewer has this output"
that I had not produced, and put a correction in my inbox for a claim I never made. The rule
product drew from it was right — a relayed statement of what someone said is the one kind of
claim the recipient cannot check — and it applies here too, in the form of a TO-BOTH message
where "you" is ambiguous across two seats.

Cheap fix, and I will adopt it myself: in a message addressed to both seats, name the seat when
attributing a finding. "The reviewer's call-site finding" and "product's STORY-1350 run" cost
three words each and remove the ambiguity entirely. I have been writing "TO ADVISOR AND PRODUCT"
and then using an unqualified "you" as well.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
